title: Course Schedule II
keyIdea: Return a topological order. Kahn: the order courses leave the indegree-0 queue is a valid order; if fewer than n come out there is a cycle → {}. Or DFS: check for a cycle, then push each course after its dependents and pop the stack.

approaches.name: DFS: cycle check, then topological sort
approaches.idea: Pass 1: dfstrack cycle check. Pass 2: post-order DFS pushes each course after everything it unlocks; reverse = order.
approaches.why: Two DFS passes, each visiting every course and edge once.

approaches.name: Kahn's algorithm (BFS on indegrees)
approaches.idea: Queue indegree-0 courses; record each one popped; lower dependents' indegrees; return the record if it has all n.
approaches.why: Each course is queued once and each edge relaxed once.

quiz.q: Why is the pop order of Kahn's queue a valid course order?
options: A course is queued only after all its prerequisites have been popped

quiz.q: When do you return an empty array?
options: When fewer than n courses were taken (there is a cycle)

quiz.q: In the DFS version, why is a course pushed AFTER its neighbours?
options: Everything that depends on it is already on the stack, so it pops out before them
No, any valid order is accepted
